qa_pair.question: What was Apple's net profit margin for fiscal year 2024, as a percentage of revenue rounded to one decimal?
qa_pair.answer: 24.0% (net income 93,736 million USD / revenue 391,035 million USD = 23.97%)

qa_pair.question: Walmart and Target both closed a fiscal year on 31 January 2026. What fiscal year label does each company's own SEC data give that period, and are the two labels the same?
qa_pair.answer: They differ by one year: Walmart labels the year ending 2026-01-31 as fiscal 2026, Target labels the year ending 2026-01-31 as fiscal 2025. Both labels are derived from the companies' own filings (fiscal_year_derived = true), not from the calendar year of the period end.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_get_concept_series(ticker="WMT", concept="revenue") -> period_end 2026-01-31, fiscal_year 2026 sec_edgar_get_concept_series(ticker="TGT", concept="revenue") -> period_end 2026-01-31, fiscal_year 2025

qa_pair.question: Apple's annual revenue series covers 19 fiscal years. How many distinct US-GAAP tags are merged to produce it, and which tag supplies the fiscal 2015 figure?
qa_pair.answer: Three tags are merged - RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, Revenues and SalesRevenueNet. Fiscal 2015 (233,715 million USD) comes from SalesRevenueNet, the pre-ASC 606 tag.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_get_concept_series(ticker="AAPL", concept="revenue", limit=25) -> resolved_concepts = the three tags above, total_periods = 19 (FY2007-FY2025) -> FY2015 point carries source_tag = "SalesRevenueNet", value 233715000000 sec_edgar_list_available_concepts(ticker="AAPL", search="revenue") confirms both tags exist for this company

qa_pair.question: For JPMorgan Chase in fiscal 2025, compare the figure returned by the "revenue" alias with the company's operating interest income. Which is larger, and by how much?
qa_pair.answer: Interest income is larger. The "revenue" alias resolves to the tag Revenues only and returns 182,447 million USD for FY2025, while InterestIncomeOperating returns 193,341 million USD - about 10,894 million USD more. For a bank the generic revenue alias does not capture the whole top line, so the tag has to be discovered rather than assumed.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_get_concept_series(ticker="JPM", concept="revenue") -> resolved_concepts ["Revenues"], FY2025 = 182447000000 sec_edgar_list_available_concepts(ticker="JPM", search="interest income") -> InterestIncomeOperating, 182 data points sec_edgar_get_concept_series(ticker="JPM", concept="InterestIncomeOperating") -> FY2025 = 193341000000

qa_pair.question: Apple's annual revenue history holds 19 periods. If only three are requested, which three fiscal years come back and how does the response say that more exist?
qa_pair.answer: The three most recent periods come back - fiscal 2023, 2024 and 2025 - not the three oldest. The response reports total_periods = 19, returned = 3 and has_more = true, so the caller can tell the series was truncated and in which direction.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_get_concept_series(ticker="AAPL", concept="revenue", limit=25) -> total_periods 19, FY2007-FY2025 sec_edgar_get_concept_series(ticker="AAPL", concept="revenue", limit=3) -> returned 3, has_more true, fiscal years 2023 / 2024 / 2025

qa_pair.question: Tesla first reported its 2017 and 2018 annual revenue, and both figures were later reported with a different value. How large were those changes, and do they amount to a restatement?
qa_pair.answer: No, they are rounding. 2017 revenue went from 11,758,751,000 to 11,759,000,000 (+249,000, about 0.002%) and 2018 from 21,461,268,000 to 21,461,000,000 (-268,000, about 0.001%). Both new values first appear in the 10-K filed 2020-02-13, accession 0001564590-20-004475, where the company began presenting figures in millions rather than thousands.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_get_fact_revisions(ticker="TSLA", concept="revenue") -> two revised periods: 2017-12-31 and 2018-12-31, each with two distinct values, second value first_reported_in 10-K filed 2020-02-13

qa_pair.question: Does Tesla's reported annual net income history contain any material restatement?
qa_pair.answer: No. Only two annual periods were ever reported with a different value - 2017 (-1,961,400,000 to -1,962,000,000) and 2018 (-976,091,000 to -976,000,000). The larger of the two is about 0.03% and both come from the same 2020 change in presentation units, so no year's result was materially restated.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_get_fact_revisions(ticker="TSLA", concept="net_income") -> periods_revised = 2, both in 2017 and 2018, change_percent below 0.05%

qa_pair.question: What aggregate market value of shares held by non-affiliates did Tesla report on the cover of its FY2025 annual report, how does it compare with the year before, and why is that figure not the company's market capitalisation?
qa_pair.answer: 892,930 million USD measured on 30 June 2025, against 550,170 million measured on 28 June 2024 - an increase of about 62%. It is not market capitalisation because the cover-page figure counts only shares held by non-affiliates: holdings of officers, directors and ten-percent owners are excluded, so true market capitalisation is higher.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_get_concept_series(ticker="TSLA", concept="public_float", period="all") -> taxonomy "dei", 2025-06-30 = 892930000000, 2024-06-28 = 550170000000 sec_edgar_list_available_concepts(ticker="TSLA", taxonomy="dei") -> confirms EntityPublicFloat is a cover-page fact

qa_pair.question: Tesla's total gross profit fell from 20,853 million USD in 2022 to 17,094 million in 2025. Which reportable segment caused the decline, and what did the other segment do?
qa_pair.answer: The automotive segment caused it: its gross profit fell from 20,565 million in 2022 to 13,292 million in 2025, a drop of 7,273 million. The energy generation and storage segment moved the other way, from 288 million to 3,802 million, adding 3,514 million. The two net to the 3,759 million decline in the group total. Segment figures are not in the XBRL API; they are in the segment note of the annual reports.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_read_filing_text(ticker="TSLA", accession_number="0001628280-26-003952", section="Segment Reporting") -> automotive gross profit 13,292 (2025) and energy 3,802 (2025) sec_edgar_read_filing_text(ticker="TSLA", accession_number="0001628280-24-002390", section="Note 18") -> automotive 20,565 and energy 288 for 2022 sec_edgar_get_concept_series(ticker="TSLA", concept="gross_profit") -> group totals agree exactly

qa_pair.question: Tesla recorded a tax benefit rather than a tax expense in 2023. What does the filing itself give as the reason, and which note carries it in the FY2023 report compared with the FY2025 report?
qa_pair.answer: The company released 6.54 billion USD of the valuation allowance on its U.S. federal and state deferred tax assets, excluding California, after concluding those assets were more likely than not to be realised. That is why the year shows a benefit of 5,001 million instead of an expense; the rate reconciliation carries it as a 5,962 million change in valuation allowance. The note is numbered 14 in the FY2023 report and 12 in the FY2025 report, so the number cannot be hardcoded across years.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_read_filing_text(ticker="TSLA", accession_number="0001628280-24-002390", section="income taxes") -> "we released $6.54 billion of our valuation allowance..."; section_matched "Note 14 - Income Taxes" sec_edgar_read_filing_text(ticker="TSLA", accession_number="0001628280-26-003952") -> available_sections lists "Note 12 - Income Taxes" sec_edgar_get_concept_series(ticker="TSLA", concept="IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit") -> FY2023 = -5001000000

qa_pair.question: Tesla published its second-quarter 2026 production and delivery figures in a form 8-K. How many vehicles did it report producing and delivering, and where inside that filing do the numbers live?
qa_pair.answer: 451,758 vehicles produced and 480,126 delivered (Model 3/Y: 442,936 produced, 467,762 delivered; other models: 8,822 and 12,364), together with 13.5 GWh of energy storage deployed. The numbers are not in the filing's primary document. The 8-K filed on 2026-07-02, accession 0001628280-26-046717, has tsla-20260702.htm as its primary document, and that file is the cover page: it states only that a press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 and incorporated by reference. The figures are in exhibit99111111.htm, 13,243 bytes, while the cover page is the larger file at 26,572 bytes.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_list_filings(ticker="TSLA", form_type="8-K") -> 2026-07-02, accession 0001628280-26-046717 sec_edgar_read_filing_text(ticker="TSLA", accession_number="0001628280-26-046717") -> cover page only; available_documents marks tsla-20260702.htm is_primary=true (26572 bytes) and lists exhibit99111111.htm (13243 bytes); the generated R1.htm (38047 bytes, the largest .htm in the directory) is excluded as XBRL-viewer output sec_edgar_read_filing_text(ticker="TSLA", accession_number="0001628280-26-046717", document="exhibit99111111.htm", max_characters=40000) -> the production/deliveries table with Total 451,758 / 480,126 sec_edgar_read_filing_text(ticker="TSLA", accession_number="0001628280-26-046717", document="exhibit99111111.htm", search="480,126") -> search_total_matches 1, hit at position 592, context showing the Total row 451,758 / 480,126; the exhibit converts to 2,080 characters in total Measured 14 Aug 2026, first from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026046717/index.json and .../exhibit99111111.htm directly, then through the tools themselves.

qa_pair.question: For the first calendar quarter of 2025, how many companies did the SEC assemble into the revenue frame, what did Apple report there, and why is Apple's figure not measured over the same days as the rest of the frame?
qa_pair.answer: The frame us-gaap/RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax/USD/CY2025Q1 holds 2,543 companies. Apple appears with 95,359,000,000 USD for the period 2024-12-29 to 2025-03-29, filed under accession 0000320193-26-000013. That period is Apple's own fiscal second quarter, not the calendar first quarter: SEC assigns each company's nearest fiscal period to a calendar frame, so period ends inside this one calendar frame range from 2025-02-23 to 2025-05-04 — about ten weeks apart. A frame is therefore a bucket of comparable-but-not-identical periods, and a company absent from it has not necessarily failed to report the concept; it may tag it differently or have no period that fits.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_compare_companies(concept="revenue", period="CY2025Q1", tickers=["AAPL"]) -> resolved_tag RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, frame CY2025Q1, frame_kind duration, Apple 95,359,000,000 with period_start 2024-12-29 and period_end 2025-03-29, and period_end_earliest / period_end_latest showing the spread sec_edgar_compare_companies(concept="total_assets", period="CY2025Q1") -> frame_requested CY2025Q1 but frame CY2025Q1I: a balance-sheet tag has no duration frame, and the instant counterpart is read instead Provenance, since these differ in strength: Apple's row and the company count (the frame's own "pts" field, 2,543) were quoted verbatim from https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/frames/us-gaap/RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax/USD/CY2025Q1.json on 14 Aug 2026. The earliest and latest period ends come from a scan of that same array rather than a verbatim quote; the tool recomputes both on every call, so they are the fields to trust over this file.

qa_pair.question: Tesla's FY2025 10-K tags some property, plant and equipment facts against a dimension. Name the axis and the member exactly as the filing writes them, say which file inside the filing carries that information, and explain why the SEC XBRL REST API cannot return it.
qa_pair.answer: The axis is us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis and the member is tsla:OperatingLeaseVehiclesMember — the member sits in Tesla's own extension namespace (http://www.tesla.com/20251231), not in us-gaap. The information lives in the XBRL instance document tsla-20251231_htm.xml, in context c-6, whose period is the instant 2025-12-31. The REST API cannot return it because SEC describes companyconcept, companyfacts and frames as aggregating facts that "apply to the entire filing entity"; a fact qualified by an axis applies to a part of the entity, so it falls outside that description. Note also what tsla-20251231_htm.xml is: SEC extracts it from the filer's inline XBRL document, so the values and contexts are the filer's while the container is SEC's.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_list_fact_dimensions(ticker="TSLA", form_type="10-K") -> axes include us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis with tsla:OperatingLeaseVehiclesMember among its members sec_edgar_get_dimensional_facts(ticker="TSLA", concept="total_assets", axis="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis") -> facts carrying context_id and fact_id, each traceable back into the instance Measured 14 Aug 2026 by fetching https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026003952/tsla-20251231_htm.xml directly; the context above was quoted verbatim from that file. The quoted SEC sentence is from https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces — SEC does not use the word "dimensional", so the conclusion drawn from it is supported inference rather than a direct statement.

qa_pair.question: Searching the full text of Tesla's 10-K filings for the word tariff, how many documents does SEC's index match, which of them was filed first, and is that first document the annual report itself?
qa_pair.answer: Twelve documents match, and SEC reports that count as exact rather than as a lower bound. The oldest was filed on 27 February 2012 under accession 0001193125-12-081990: the file d279413dex1050.htm, which SEC describes as "SUPPLY AGREEMENT". It is an exhibit inside a 10-K submission, not the annual report itself — the match is a document, not a filing. The eleven other matches are the annual reports for fiscal years 2015 through 2025 with the exception of fiscal years 2012, 2013 and 2014, whose reports are absent from the result.
qa_pair.verification: sec_edgar_search_filings(query="\"tariff\"", form_type="10-K", ticker="TSLA", limit=100) -> total_matching = 12, total_is_exact = true -> the hit with the earliest filing_date is accession_number 0001193125-12-081990, document d279413dex1050.htm, filing_date 2012-02-27, description "SUPPLY AGREEMENT" Measured 15 Aug 2026 by fetching https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22tariff%22&forms=10-K&ciks=0001318605 directly and reading all twelve hits; the identifiers and dates above are quoted from that response, in which hits.total was {"value":12,"relation":"eq"}. This answer moves as Tesla files further annual reports that use the word, so the count is the part to re-measure before treating a mismatch as a regression.
